title: But what is a neural network?
subject: CS / ML
beats: Shows a blurry 28x28 three and asks you to notice how effortlessly you read it
Flips it: writing a program for the same task goes from trivial to daunting
Promises the structure will feel motivated, assuming no background; learning comes next video
A neuron is only a thing that holds a number between 0 and 1
784 input neurons hold pixel brightness; the number is named activation
10 output neurons, one per digit; hidden layers left as a deliberate question mark
Admits two layers of 16 is an arbitrary choice made to fit the screen
Activations in one layer cause the next, loosely like neurons firing
Runs an image through a trained net; brightest output neuron is the answer
Asks what middle layers might hope to do; digits are loops and lines
Hope: each neuron detects a part like an upper loop, built from little edges
Flags that the trained net may not really do this; will revisit
Layers of abstraction also fit speech: sounds, syllables, words, phrases
Asks you to design the layer-to-layer mechanism: what knobs would it need?
Weights on each connection, weighted sum, shown as a green/red pixel grid
Negative weights around a bright strip turn the neuron into an edge detector
Sum can be any number, so squish it into 0-1 with the sigmoid
Want activity only above 10? Add a bias before squishing
Every neuron repeats this: 784x16 weights, about 13,000 knobs in all
Learning means finding the knob settings; imagine setting them all by hand
Cumbersome sum rewritten as matrix-vector product plus bias vector, sigmoid outside
Refines neuron to a function; the whole network is one 784-to-10 function
Complexity is reassuring; next video shows how the weights are learned
Subscribe joke about recommendation networks, Patreon thanks
Guest researcher: sigmoid is old school, modern nets use ReLU
